claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser sintering can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing controlled porosity via selective laser sintering can reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Porosity can be introduced without sacrificing the room-temperature mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr.
Porosity can be introduced without sacrificing the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr up to 1000 °C.
Pore size and pore distribution are the structural mediators of the proposed response.
A continuous load-bearing network of high-entropy-alloy phases is retained after controlled porosity is introduced.
Retention of a continuous load-bearing alloy network maintains strength despite the introduced porosity.
The porous material is predicted to have maintained or slightly reduced strength relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed performance boundary extends from room temperature to 1000 °C.
The proposed performance boundary covers both tensile and compressive loading.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, whereas the predicted outcome permits slightly reduced strength.
The claim of no sacrifice is inconsistent with a falsification rule that accepts strength losses of up to 20%.
The mechanism says strength is maintained, while the predicted outcome also allows strength to be reduced.
